summary.text: Darya Farivar is a Democratic member of the Washington House of Representatives from District 46-Position 2, where she has served since January 2023, and she is on the November 3, 2026 general election ballot seeking re-election.
Before joining the Legislature she worked in disability rights advocacy.

paragraphs.text: Darya Farivar was born and raised in the Lake City neighborhood of Seattle's 46th Legislative District, according to the House Democrats' biography, and graduated from Roosevelt High School.
She earned a B.A. in communicative disorders from the University of Redlands, with a minor in women, gender and sexuality studies.

Before the Legislature, Farivar worked in disability rights advocacy focused on behavioral health, housing and the criminal legal system, and earlier on supporting immigrants and refugees with developmental disabilities.

Her community involvement has included serving as a founding board member of the Washington Coalition for Police Accountability, co-chair of the Seattle Women's Commission and policy chair of the Washington State Special Education Advisory Council.
She took office in the House on January 9, 2023, and her biography describes her as the first Middle Eastern woman and first Iranian American woman elected to the Washington State Legislature.
